channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: China Wants Its Data to Power the World’s A.I.
item.description: China is exporting more than A.I. models. It wants its data to influence the world’s chatbots, raising fears that Beijing’s narratives will spread with the technology.

item.title: NPR: Hayden Panettiere, who starred in 'Heroes' and 'Nashville,' dies at 36
item.description: A child actor since she was cast in various commercials as an 11-month-old, Panettiere was best known for her role as the country music star Juliette Barnes in the series "Nashville."

item.title: BBC News: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told
item.description: Mothers, like Katy, describe battles to make ex-partners pay, while fathers say they have been wrongly charged thousands.

item.description: With heatwaves now recognised as disasters, personal testimonies are key to a new project that looks to protect those living in the most cramped districts of India’s capital Every summer evening, Gulshan follows the same…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Inside the UK’s ‘stressful’ cost of living crisis Burnham hopes to tackle
item.description: Britain's new premier has promised to ease the suffering of millions of families unable to afford basic items.

item.title: Ars Technica: Wildfire smoke now bigger prenatal threat than human sources of air pollution
item.description: Regulations reduced prenatal exposure to harmful emissions, but wildfire smoke is erasing gains.

item.title: WIRED Science: El Niño and Saharan Dust Silence Atlantic Hurricane Season
item.description: El Niño coupled with Saharan dust is making this year’s hurricane season a dud. But there’s still potential for dangerous storms.

item.title: WIRED Business: The Next Big Influencer Is This 4-Foot-Tall Robot From China
item.description: The Unitree G1 has found online fame as a relatively affordable robot that can charm a crowd. But can it ever hold down a real job?

item.title: The New Yorker: The Big, Dumb, Gluttonous Fun of America’s Semiquincentennial
item.description: In D.C. and the Dakotas, at rodeos and powwows, celebrating the country means taking in pride and disappointment and fellow-feeling.
